title: Advanced HTML
description: Master advanced HTML: meta tags for SEO, Open Graph for social sharing, custom data attributes, HTML entities, microdata, and HTML5 browser APIs.
learningObjectives: Write complete SEO meta tags and Open Graph markup
Add favicons and web app manifests
Use data-* attributes to store custom data
Type special characters using HTML entities
Understand microdata and Schema.org for rich results

sections.content: The <head> — Your SEO Command Center
Everything inside <head> is metadata — information for browsers and search engines, not users. Getting this right is the easiest win for SEO.

<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
  <title>Python for Beginners — CodeBuddy (50-60 chars max)</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Learn Python in 40 hours with 100 interactive exercises on CodeBuddy. Free to start." />
  <meta name="robots" content="index, follow" />
  <link rel="canonical" href="https://codebuddy.dev/learn/python" />
</head>
🎯 Title: 50-60 chars. Description: 150-160 chars. Every page needs unique values.

exercises.question: What is the recommended maximum character length for a meta description?
exercises.explanation: Google truncates meta descriptions at ~155-160 characters. Write compelling descriptions within this limit.

sections.content: Control How Your Page Looks on Social Media
Open Graph tags tell Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, and Slack exactly what image, title, and description to show when someone shares your link.

<meta property="og:type" content="website" />
<meta property="og:url" content="https://codebuddy.dev/" />
<meta property="og:title" content="CodeBuddy — Learn to Code" />
<meta property="og:description" content="100+ interactive coding lessons." />
<meta property="og:image" content="https://codebuddy.dev/og.jpg" />

<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
<meta name="twitter:title" content="CodeBuddy — Learn to Code" />
<meta name="twitter:image" content="https://codebuddy.dev/og.jpg" />
🎯 OG images should be 1200×630px. Test at https://metatags.io

exercises.question: What are the recommended dimensions for an Open Graph image?
exercises.explanation: 1200×630px is the standard OG image size used by all major social platforms without cropping.

sections.content: Storing Data in HTML with data-*
Any attribute starting with data- is valid on any HTML element. JavaScript reads them via element.dataset. Perfect for storing widget config, analytics tracking data, or cart item info.
Wireless Earbuds

exercises.question: Create a user card div with data-user-id='u123', data-role='admin', data-points='850'. Include an h3 with 'coder42' and a span with 'Admin'.
exercises.explanation: data-* attributes are a clean way to embed structured data in HTML for JavaScript consumption.

sections.content: HTML Entities
Special characters that have meaning in HTML syntax must be escaped using entities: < for <, > for >, & for &, © for ©,   for a non-breaking space.

Use <p> for paragraphs.

© 2025 CodeBuddy. All rights reserved.

Price: $9.99 — billed monthly.
Favicon

<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" />
<link rel="icon" type="image/png" sizes="32x32" href="/icon-32.png" />
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/apple-touch-icon.png" />

exercises.question: Which HTML entity displays the copyright symbol ©?
exercises.explanation: © renders ©. All entities start with & and end with ;.

sections.content: Structured Data for Rich Search Results

Structured data tells Google the exact meaning of your content. Result: star ratings, FAQs, breadcrumbs, and event details shown directly in search results (rich results). JSON-LD is the recommended format.

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Course",
  "name": "Python for Beginners",
  "description": "Learn Python in 40 hours.",
  "provider": {
    "@type": "Organization",
    "name": "CodeBuddy"
  }
}
</script>
🎯 Test with Google's Rich Results Test: https://search.google.com/test/rich-results

exercises.question: Which format does Google recommend for adding structured data?
hints: It keeps structured data separate from HTML markup
exercises.explanation: Google recommends JSON-LD because it's easy to add/update without touching visible HTML markup.
